source_edition: January 2013 modified / 2014 corrected CDE electronic edition
source_cautions: 5.NF.7 source spans printed pages 37 and 38; footnote explicitly excludes general fraction-by-fraction division.
5.NF.5 greater-than/less-than multiplier intuition must not be interpreted as a universal inequality for negative base quantities.
5.G.2 requires first-quadrant point graphing, not all-four-quadrant mastery.
5.MD.5 prism formulas are scoped to whole-number edge lengths; composite prism volume concerns non-overlapping parts.

rows.author_mathematical_scope: Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with unlike denominators by replacing them with equivalent fractions sharing a denominator.
Solve same-whole fraction addition/subtraction word problems, including unlike denominators; use models or equations and benchmark-fraction estimates to check reasonableness.
Interpret a/b as a divided by b and solve whole-number division situations giving fraction or mixed-number results, supported by models or equations.

Multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction: interpret (a/b)×q as a equal parts of q/b and as a×q÷b; find fractional-side rectangular areas by tiling and multiplying lengths. For 5.NF.4.b, tile with unit squares whose side lengths are appropriate unit fractions, demonstrate the tiled area equals the product of rectangle side lengths, and represent products of fractions as rectangular areas.
required_material_conditions: subpart a: interpret fraction times quantity and sequence a×q÷b
subpart b: area of rectangles with fractional side lengths
5.NF.4.b: tile using squares with appropriate unit-fraction side lengths
5.NF.4.b: fractional products represented by rectangular areas

rows.author_mathematical_scope: Reason about multiplication as scaling: compare product magnitude to a factor without computing, explain the Grade 5 context of fractional multipliers above and below one, and connect fraction equivalence to multiplication by one.
required_material_conditions: subpart a: comparative factor-size reasoning without computation
multiplication by one and fraction equivalence
nonnegative Grade 5 context; do not universalize greater/less inequalities to negative numbers

rows.author_mathematical_scope: Solve real-world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers using suitable visual models or equations.

For 5.NF.7.a, interpret and compute a unit fraction divided by a nonzero whole number using a story context, visual fraction model and multiplication-division relationship. For 5.NF.7.b, interpret and compute a whole number divided by a unit fraction with a model and justified relationship. For 5.NF.7.c, solve real-world word problems for both forms with diagrams and equations. General fraction-by-fraction division is not required in Grade 5.
required_material_conditions: 5.NF.7.a: unit fraction divided by nonzero whole number with context, visual model and multiplication-division explanation
5.NF.7.b: whole number divided by unit fraction with visual model and justification
5.NF.7.c: real-world word problems for both forms with diagrams and equations
source footnote: general fraction divided by fraction not required

rows.author_mathematical_scope: Convert between different-sized standard units of measure within one measurement system and use conversions in multistep real-world problems.
Construct line plots of measurement data in halves, quarters and eighths of a unit; apply grade-level fraction operations to interpret and solve problems from the plots.
Recognize volume as an attribute of three-dimensional solids: a unit-side cube has one cubic unit of volume, and gap-free, overlap-free packing by n unit cubes gives n cubic units.
required_material_conditions: subpart a: unit cube = one cubic unit
subpart b: packing without gaps or overlaps

rows.author_mathematical_scope: Measure volumes by counting unit cubes, including cubic centimeters, inches, feet, and improvised units.
Solve prism-volume problems by connecting packing cubes to multiplication of whole-number edge lengths and V=l×w×h or V=B×h; add non-overlapping prism volumes for composite solids.
required_material_conditions: subpart a: unit-cube packing and volume as threefold whole-number product
subpart b: right rectangular prisms with whole-number edges and both formulas
subpart c: two non-overlapping prisms and additive volume

rows.author_mathematical_scope: Define a coordinate plane using perpendicular axes intersecting at a zero origin; locate points by ordered pairs and distinguish x-coordinate direction from y-coordinate direction.
Represent mathematical and real-world situations by graphing points in the first quadrant and interpreting coordinates in context.
Explain that properties belonging to a two-dimensional figure category also apply to its nested subcategories (for example squares inherit properties of rectangles).
Classify two-dimensional figures in hierarchies based on their defining properties.
